controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body color at its measured dayside temperature, 2,360 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of 55 Cnc e's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 4.5 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

controls.label: Illustration
controls.qualification: An artist's surface from NASA's 55 Cnc e 3D model; not an observation.
controls.notes: NASA's illustration of 55 Cnc e, from its 3D model. Nobody has resolved this planet's disc, so none of the color or features in it was observed. Its longitudes are arbitrary.

controls.label: Climate model
controls.qualification: Simulation · Isca · Zhan & Koll (2026) · False color
controls.notes: Air temperature at 5 bar of 55 Cnc e in the Isca simulation of Zhan & Koll (2026): a model, not a measurement. The run assumes a cloud-free atmosphere of pure carbon dioxide, 10 bar at the surface, on a planet that keeps one face to its star. The map is the run's long-term mean at half the surface pressure, the level the paper's Figure 1 draws. Nobody has detected a 10-bar carbon dioxide atmosphere on 55 Cnc e. Webb's eclipse spectra show an atmosphere of carbon monoxide or carbon dioxide (Hu et al. 2024); this paper finds they fit thick, carbon-dioxide-rich ones like this best. Gray caps: no released grid samples beyond 87.9° north or south. The false color runs from 500 to 3,500 K; it is not what an eye would see. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

controls.label: Steam model
controls.qualification: Simulation · Isca · Zhan & Koll (2026) · False color
controls.notes: Air temperature at 0.05 bar of 55 Cnc e in the Isca simulation of Zhan & Koll (2026): a model, not a measurement. The run assumes a cloud-free atmosphere of pure water vapor, 10 bar at the surface, on a planet that keeps one face to its star. The map is the run's long-term mean at 0.005 of the surface pressure, the level the paper's Figure 1 draws, since the deep air is all one temperature. Nobody has detected a water vapor atmosphere on 55 Cnc e. The paper finds this case fits Webb's eclipse spectra only at the edge of its cutoff, worse than carbon-dioxide-rich ones. Gray caps: no released grid samples beyond 85.8° north or south. The false color runs from 500 to 3,500 K; it is not what an eye would see. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: The orbits of 55 Cnc's planets in this map from above, to scale, with 55 Cnc e highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

55 Cnc e's transmission spectrum: the fraction of starlight the planet blocks as it crosses its star, larger where its atmosphere absorbs. 25 measured bins from Tsiaras et al. 2016 (Hubble Space Telescope satellite, Wide Field Camera 3), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors.

55 Cnc e crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (44, 46, 72) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 332064670, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 6-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
